newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein leader's UK parliament visit attacked.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein leader's UK parliament visit attacked.

text.p: A private visit to Britain's parliament by Irish republican leader Gerry Adams drew heavy criticism on Wednesday and the Labour opposition condemned one of its own legislators for inviting the Sinn Fein leader.
Adams had hoped to launch his autobiography in the building of the House of Commons on Thursday. But the launch was cancelled by parliamentary officials over the weekend.
Left-wing member of parliament Jeremy Corbyn, however, announced he would host a private meeting with Adams instead.

Labour officials said they might throw Corbyn out of the party if the meeting took place in parliament. Sinn Fein is the political wing of the Irish Republican Army (IRA), which has fought to oust Britain from Northern Ireland. "We utterly condemn his proposed action. If he persists it will be a matter for disciplinary action," said Donald Dewar, Labour's chief parliamentary business manager. "It is particularly reprehensible in the light of recent events involving the IRA," Dewar said.
On Monday, British police foiled what they said was an imminent IRA bomb attack, arresting five people in London.
Adams later said he had never intended to launch his book in the House of Commons, but had hoped to meet Corbyn and then hold a news conference.

"I would like to think they're not afraid of ideas and not afraid of their members of parliament discussing...how a peace process can be put together," Adams told reporters in Dublin while launching the book -- "Before the Dawn" -- in Ireland.

"I'm very disappointed, despite the British Labour party's disgraceful record, that they're even against dialogue." Adams was elected MP for West Belfast in the 1980s but never took his seat in the House of Commons (lower house). He said he regarded Britain as an occupying power in the province and has refused to take an oath of allegiance to the British monarch.
He has visited parliament several times in the past few years since as a former legislator he cannot be barred.
